props.title: How to reproof waxed cotton
props.description: Once a year, 40 minutes, a hair dryer. Here's the whole process.
props.author: Ballard repair
paragraphs: Waxed cotton sheds water because the fibers are coated, not because the weave is tight. The coating wears off at the shoulders, cuffs, and anywhere a strap rubs. When water stops beading and starts soaking in, it's time.

You need a tin of reproofing wax, a clean cloth, and a hair dryer. Brush the jacket clean and let it dry fully. Warm the wax tin in hot water until the surface is soft. Work the wax in with the cloth in small circles, thin coats, paying attention to seams and the worn areas. Then go over the whole jacket with the hair dryer so the wax melts into the weave instead of sitting on top.
Hang it overnight somewhere warm. It'll feel tacky for a day and smell like wax for a week. If you'd rather not, send it to us. Reproofing is $35 and takes about two weeks.
